utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-00-39-A, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, could you please tell me that you can hear me in a language you understand, and for the record state your name. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Momcilo Krajisnik. I can follow the proceedings in my language. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krajisnik. Appearances, the Prosecution first.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: Your Honour, Peter Kremer appearing for the Prosecution. With me is Katharina Margetts and our case manager Lourdes Galicia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kremer. Now let's hope that the teleconference link will function correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Alan Dershowitz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This is what I have been looking forward to, hearing your voice, Mr. Dershowitz. Can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] I can hear you well. Thank you very much, Your Honour. It's Alan Dershowitz calling from Massachusetts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Very good. I'm pleased to have you with us. Now, Ms. Butler and Ms. Whitaker appearing on behalf of the amicus and who are also in attendance via teleconference. Ms. Butler, Michelle Butler, and Quincy Whitaker, can you hear me? Your voice sounds very weak. Could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. Can you hear us now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, I can, just barely. Let's hope that by the time we get back to you, the sound will be a bit stronger. So thank you all. This, as you know, is a Status Conference called in accordance with Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. Rule 65 bis (B) requires a Status Conference to be convened within 120 days of the last Status Conference to allow any person in custody, pending appeals, the opportunity to raise issues in relation thereto including the mental and physical condition of that person. The last Status Conference in this case was held on 31 March, 2008. I would like to begin this Status Conference by inquiring into Mr. Krajisnik's health. Mr. Krajisnik, I would like you to respond on this issue, and now you have -- you will have a chance later on in the Status Conference to address other issues if necessary, but right now I would like you just to speak to any concerns you have regarding your physical or mental well being. Mr. Krajisnik. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I feel well, Judge. Thank you for asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it you have no other physical or mental issues you would like to raise with me, and I am pleased to know that you are well and that everything is well. Now, you may sit down, Mr. Krajisnik. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now, I want to say a few words to the parties and to the representatives of amicus about scheduling. I note that the Scheduling Order for the appeals hearing was filed on the 18th of July, 2008. The appeals hearing is scheduled to be held on Thursday, 21 August 2008, in Courtroom I, from 8.30 a.m. through 1730. Mr. Krajisnik, let me ask you to clarify an issue in relation to the appeals hearing. Will Mr. Dershowitz be arguing the JCE issue during the hearing, or will you do it yourself? That's a question to you, Mr. Krajisnik. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Judge, I'm pleased that Mr. Dershowitz is taking part in these proceedings. I hope that he will present the position involved. What I can say is that we have agreed that at the final hearing, he will present his view regarding joint criminal enterprise and other matters, of course, that are related to joint criminal enterprise. What I find a bit surprising is the fact that I hadn't heard of this date earlier on, the 21st of August. This is the first time I hear of it. I assume that this is the first time that Mr. Dershowitz hears of it. However, I kindly ask you, since he is present, we have him on the telephone, could he please say whether he will be in a position to attend this final hearing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Krajisnik. As I have mentioned to you, the Scheduling Order was filed on the 18th of July. I would have assumed that it would have been communicated to you right away as well as to Mr. Dershowitz; but before I turn to Mr. Dershowitz, let me make some additional comments and then I will turn to him. So you can sit down, please. I would like to note here that pursuant to our decision, the Appeals Chamber's decision of the 28th of February, 2008, the scope of Mr. Dershowitz's representation of Mr. Krajisnik is limited to the issue of JCE. That limitation applies also to Mr. Dershowitz's arguments during the hearing. Furthermore, I note that under the Scheduling Order of 18 July 2008, Mr. Dershowitz is not allocated any additional time. What this means is that Mr. Dershowitz and Mr. Krajisnik must decide between themselves how to use the time allocated to the Scheduling Order -- in the Scheduling Order for submissions by the appellant. There is one further issue relating to scheduling that I would like to note, and this pertains to Mr. Krajisnik's Rule 115 motion. The Appeals Chamber is currently seized of the appellant's motion together with a supplement pursuant to Rule 115 of the Rules, by which he seeks to present additional evidence before the Chamber. Last Friday, 18 of July, the Prosecution responded to this motion. The Pre-Appeal Judge - that's, of course, me - has granted both the appellant's and the Prosecution's request to exceed the word limits. I understand the process of translation of the documents the appellant seeks to have admitted has been completed today, Mr. Nemitz, that is correct? Today, that is on the 21st of July, 2008. So, all the documents, by now, have been now translated. The appellant, if he so wishes, will have to reply to the Prosecution's response within 14 days after he has received the B/C/S translation of the response. Mr. Krajisnik, and I would like to remind you, please, that if you choose to file a reply, you are required to respect the word limit, which is limited to 3.000 words for a reply in the case of Rule 115 motion. As you know, we have been quite generous in regards to your exceeding the word limits last time, but I must ask you this time, please, comply with the Rules. Considering this schedule, the Appeals Chamber will try to render its decision on the appellant's Rule 115 motion and on the supplement prior to the appeal hearing on 21 August 2008. And, at this point, I would like to ask the parties and the representatives of amicus whether they have any other issues that they would like to raise at this time. Let me start from Mr. Kremer for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: We have nothing to raise, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krajisnik, do you have any other issues you would like to raise at this spot, or you would prefer me to go directly to Mr. Dershowitz? THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Judge, I would just like to ask, if possible, that before the 21st of August, I meet with Mr. Dershowitz because my appeal is closely linked to joint criminal enterprise and the arguments involved in that. When you speak to Mr. Dershowitz, I do hope that you will take that into consideration and that such a decision can be made. Certainly, it is the registry that is supposed to pay for Mr. Dershowitz's visit because it would be appropriate for us to meet before the 21st.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm afraid we have to wait a second for technical problems. The line to Mr. Dershowitz at the moment is waiting to be resuscitated.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Hello. Hello.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Dershowitz, can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Hello.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Dershowitz, I can hear your voice, can you hear mine?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] I can, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Great. Did you hear the comments made by Mr. Krajisnik, that he was --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] I did, but I did not hear the comments made by Judge Meron.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I think that as regards the desire of Mr. Krajisnik to meet with you, this is between the two of you. You are his counsel, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- you have the right to meet with him. There is no problem that I can see about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now, regarding the subquestion of payment for your trip to The Hague, it has always been understood, Mr. Dershowitz, that you are counsel of Mr. Krajisnik under Rule 44, I believe; and in these circumstances, all the financial implications pertaining to your participation in the case, on accomodation, travel, et cetera, are imputed to Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] That's not an issue that I wanted to raise. I'm perfectly satisfied with whatever arrangement the Court makes. My concern is that I received no notice until just now of an argument on the 21st of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] And it's not a date that is available to me. Is that a firm date? I just, as I said, I just received the notice in the oral discussion. I had never heard of the 21st before being a date for argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, the Appeals Chamber issued a Scheduling Order on Friday, and it was my sort of expectation that you would have been -- this would have been communicated to you without any delay; but, of course, there is not too much difference between Friday and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And that order is, I'm afraid, quite firm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] It is firm. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This is one day only, and I hope that whatever other arrangements you have, it would be possible for you to come because this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] The other issue is that the Court has not yet, as I understand it, ruled on Mr. Krajisnik's 115 motion that we were hoping to incorporate in the appeal because it relates to the JCE issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, you heard my comments on that a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] I did not, no. The phone went dead and I did not hear your comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Okay. So what I will do is repeat what I said here on the record, okay?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: It's good that you have warned me about that. Here is what I told the court a moment ago, and I will repeat it verbatim for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: There is one further issue relating to scheduling that I would like to note with respect to Mr. Krajisnik's 115 motion. The Appeals Chamber is currently seized of the appellant's motion together with a supplement pursuant to Rule 115 of the Rules, by which he seekers to present additional evidence before the Chamber. Last Friday, 18th of July, the Prosecution responded to this motion. The Pre-Appeal Judge has granted both the appellant's and the Prosecution's requests to exceed the word limit. The Appeals Chamber has been advised that the translation of the documents that the appellant seeks to have admitted as additional evidence has been completed today, by the 21st of July, 2008. The appellant, if he so wishes, will have time to reply to the Prosecution's response, and he would have to do so within 14 days after he has received the B/C/S translation of the response. I reminded Mr. Krajisnik of his obligation to strictly adhere to the word limit. You know, Mr. Dershowitz, that we have granted his request --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- for a rather significant excess of the word limit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes. And I want to advise the Court that I am not aware that he submitted this in excess of the word limit, and it was done completely by him on a pro se basis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I'm certainly not attributing this to you, Mr. Dershowitz. I understand that. So, I concluded my comments on the Rule 115 motion by saying that the Appeals Chamber will try, and I'm optimistic about it, to render its decision on the appellant's Rule 115 motion and on the supplement prior to the appeal hearing on 21 August 2008, so that you, Mr. Dershowitz, when you prepare your comments for the hearing would be able to base yourself on a definite ruling by the Appeals Chamber regarding the status of those additional documents, additional evidence that Mr. Krajisnik wanted to have admitted under Rule 115.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Thank you very much, Your Honour. Do you know whether we will have an opportunity to respond briefly in writing and supplement our submissions in writing after the Chamber renders its decision on the Rule 115.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: No, that will be the end of the story on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] It will be oral, just oral presentations?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Oh, you mean during the hearing?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: I did not quite understand you. You respond briefly in writing and supplement your submissions on what precisely? I mean, that would not be any kind of an appeal on our ruling, would it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Well, since I don't have the ruling yet, it's unclear. But let's assume that there is a ruling that is adverse to Mr. Krajisnik and one that's relevant on the appeal. I would be permitted, I imagine, to incorporate that in the argument I'm making on the 21st of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: In your oral argument, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] But not in writing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, let's cross that bridge when we come to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: If there is a motion that you would like to submit prior to the hearing, I don't think that this would fit into the schedule of briefings envisaged by the Rules, but we will look at it if you submit something.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] I understand. That seems eminently fair. Can you also tell me, Your Honour, how much time will be allocated to my argument on the JCE?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: This was another matter which I mentioned in my comments earlier today which, unfortunately, because of telecommunication problems, you could not hear. I referred to the fact that your representation is, of course, limited to the issue of JCE.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And that limitation applies also to your arguments during the hearing that we have announced. And as stated in the Scheduling Order of 18th July 2008, which I understand has not yet reached you and I would ask the registry to make absolutely sure that another copy of that is faxed to Mr. Dershowitz -- excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Dershowitz, I am told by my colleagues from the registry that an e-mail was sent to all the parties, including yourself, on the 18th, transmitting the full text of that Scheduling Order. In any event, we did say in that Scheduling Order that you and Mr. Krajisnik must decide between yourselves how to use the time allocated in the Scheduling Order for submissions by Mr. Krajisnik. So we just work it out with Mr. Krajisnik how much of his allotted time you take --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- how much will be left to him. And we cannot grant additional time to you or to Mr. Krajisnik, but you have, I think, enough time within the parameters established by the Scheduling Order to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] That sounds fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Anything else that you would like to raise, Mr. Dershowitz?

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] I think not. I'm sorry that my office did not seem to receive or certainly didn't communicate to me the e-mail, so this did take me a little bit by surprise. So I come less prepared to this hearing than I would like to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I think you caught up very nicely.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] I appreciate that. I don't know, but I'm sure it's in the order, how much time totally Mr. Krajisnik and I will have to present his case. Does amicus also have time to present? Do we have to divide it among three?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: No. You don't have to divide it among three. I think the amicus got 30 minutes or something like that, but I don't want to --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] That's okay. I don't want to take the Court's time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: The amicus has 30 minutes, and there will be response by the Prosecution to him, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] How much do we have to reply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Well, I think it would be better if you would read the Scheduling Order, but, as an exceptional measure of technical assistance, let me --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- let me read a few words from the Scheduling Order. Submissions of the appellant, one hour and 30 minutes, then there is the opposed, then appellant has another 30 minutes, so it's two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Now, given your experience in American courts, I'm sure you will consider this to be quite generous --

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] It is quite generous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: -- since in the US Supreme Court, you would not get that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] No. It will only the last 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And, Mr. Dershowitz, I think, if you have nothing else to raise, let me thank you for your participation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DERSHOWITZ
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Thank you. I'm sorry for the difficulty, and I look forward to being in the court on the 21st of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And very much look forward to seeing you then. Good-bye. I think we now turn to amicus, right? Ms. Butler, Ms. Whitaker, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Do you have any issues on behalf of the amicus that you would like to raise? And let me first make sure that you did receive a copy of the Scheduling Order which we issued on Friday.

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes, we did. Thank you, Your Honour. Just one matter we'd like to raise, and that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: It's terribly difficult to hear you. It's terribly, terribly weak. Try to raise your voice as much as you can.

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Can you hear me now, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Sort of, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] There is just one matter. We received the Scheduling Order. There was just one matter we wished to raise and that is can we clarify when it is anticipated that the translation of the Prosecution's response to Mr. Krajisnik's Rule 115 motion is anticipated that will be received in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Kremer, when is your response anticipated? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: The B/C/S version is in the hands of the registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: That is the response which I mentioned, and why wouldn't the amicus be aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: The amicus is asking the question as to when the B/C/S version of the Prosecution's response will be available to Mr. Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KREMER
utterances.text: That's the way I heard the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You're quite right. Ms. Michelle, please wait a second. We are checking that with the registry.

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, the Prosecution responded last Friday. While waiting for the response, is there anything else that you would like to raise, or that's the only question that you have?

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] No, Your Honour. It would be the times of the B/C/S translation of Mr. Krajisnik's motion prior to the 21st of August. Otherwise, we have no other issues to raise. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's give it another second and see if we can get some kind of tentative answer to you. Yes, I now have heard from the registry that the B/C/S translation will be received on the 29th of July, 2008. Could you hear me?

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour. That is sufficient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, the 29th. So this answers your question. If I understand your question correctly, this is the only question you wanted to raise with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. WHITAKER
utterances.text: [Via telephone conference] Yes. Mr. Krajisnik has sufficient time to respond after the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Yes, he will. Thank you very much, and I believe let me just again check with Mr. Krajisnik whether he would like to raise anything more. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since I haven't received the scheduling - in fact, I have received a visit from my family - it's possible that someone has put it in my room today, but I haven't seen it. So I'm giving this answer with a sort of reservation now. What I have gathered just now, if you can confirm that for me, the total time for the presentation of the Defence case prepared by myself and Mr. Dershowitz would be one and a half hours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Two hours. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] -- with 30 minutes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: It would be two hours. You will have a little break in the meantime to rest. Altogether it will be two hours, and that time you have to allocate, to divide, distribute it between yourself and Mr. Dershowitz. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] I was a little bit confused by the time allocated. I heard from other appellants that the time was longer. So this is only two hours available for the presentation of the Defence case by myself and Mr. Dershowitz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: You will later in the day have an opportunity to respond to the Prosecution's appeal, but I'm speaking about your own basic case. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I understand. So Mr. Dershowitz and I have in total two hours to present our appeal before the Appellate Chamber, and that will be an oral presentation .

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: That is correct. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And, again, please remember that you will have other opportunities during the day to reply to the statement by the Prosecution, and you will have additional 30 plus 20 minutes during the day, which are in addition to what I mentioned. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] So the additional 20 or 30 minutes is in excess of two hours, and that would be a rejoinder to the Prosecution's argument, if I understand correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: Mr. Krajisnik, you will find, in the Detention Unit, the Scheduling Order. You don't need me to read it to you again. Everything is very clear in it. THE APPELLANT: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MERON
utterances.text: And I just want to make quite sure that you understand that you -- that the time allocated to you is normal time and that you are not treated any less favourably than anybody else. I think that this would conclude our business of today. Unless I hear any comments from Mr. Dershowitz or Ms. Whitaker in London or from the Prosecution or from Mr. Krajisnik, I will conclude our proceedings for today. We'll call the hearing closed, and I thank the parties, the amicus, Mr. Dershowitz, the interpreters, and the entire staff for their help in arranging this meeting. After all, the communications did function at least adequately. So I thank you.
